title: Feedback dynamics in matching networks drive behavioral differentiation despite overlapping objectives
summary: Many bipartite social networks exhibit pronounced asymmetries in selectivity and matching opportunities: members of one side can afford to be highly selective, while members of the opposite side are forced to accept less desirable matches. While it is natural to try to explain this asymmetry in terms of the intrinsic characteristics of the two sides or other exogenous factors, here we show that such asymmetries can also emerge endogenously through a feedback process generated by the matching process itself: as one side becomes more selective, the other side is pushed to be less selective due…
